newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares edge higher, seen well supported.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares edge higher, seen well supported.

text.p: Austrian shares ended in positive territory on Monday, helped by a record close in Germany, a stable dollar and a strong bond market, traders said.

Market participants added that technical buying had pushed selected shares, including Vienna airport company Flughafen Wien and regional utility EVN, higher towards the close. Overall volume was down partly due to a holiday in London.
"It was a fairly uneventful session with very little movement," a trader said. He forecast that the market's late strength would carry into Tuesday, however.
The blue-chip ATX index finished 5.95 points, or 0.49 percent, higher at 1,211.65, rebounding from an early low of 1,203.34.
Overall 12 shares closed up, eight down and one unchanged.
Leading gainer was Flughafen Wien, which advanced 29 schillings, or 5.86 percent, to 531 schillings.

Preferred shares in bank Creditanstalt were the biggest decliner, down 7.5 schillings, or 1.64 percent, at 453 schillings. Traders noted that Creditanstalt shares had come under some pressure after going ex-dividend.
Oil firm OMV climbed 8.9 schillings to 1,338.80 after reporting strong first quarter earnings and giving an upbeat assessment for the full-year.
Water treatment company BWT continued its strong gains since the start of the year, helped by an 18 percent rise in first quarter net profit. BWT shares closed 23 schillings higher at 1,700.
ATX May futures stood 17 points up at 1,211.0. The all-share Vienna bourse index gained 1.98 points to end at 456.72. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 254
